description: Accessibility Explorer — inspect and interact with native desktop accessibility trees from any running application. Users connect to a window by title, process ID, or 'Desktop', capture the accessibility tree via the Rust-native UIA (Windows), AT-SPI (Linux), or AX (macOS) adapter, browse elements in a hierarchical tree view with role-coded badges and expand/collapse, view full element properties and state flags, execute actions (Click, Focus, Type) via native accessibility patterns, query the tree by role/label/interactivity, and preview the AI Context output that workflow agents receive when using native_accessibility steps.

groups.name: Page Structure and Layout
groups.description: The Accessibility Explorer has a vertical layout: header bar with title and status, connection bar (when disconnected), stats bar (when connected), a two-column main area (60% tree view, 40% details panel), and a bottom tabbed section for Query and AI Context. When disconnected, only the header, connection input, and an empty-state message are visible.

assertions.description: The page header displays 'Accessibility Explorer' as an h2 heading with an Accessibility icon

When connected with a captured tree, the main content area shows a two-column layout: left column (flex-3, ~60%) containing the Tree View card, and right column (flex-2, ~40%) containing the Details card. Both columns have scroll areas for overflow.
assertions.precondition: Connected to a target with a captured tree

assertions.description: When not connected, the page shows the text 'Connect to an application to explore its accessibility tree' centered in the main area, with no tree or details visible

groups.name: Connection and Target Selection
groups.description: Users connect to a desktop application by entering its window title (e.g., 'Notepad'), process ID (e.g., 'pid:1234'), or 'Desktop' for the entire desktop. The Connect button establishes the accessibility bridge via the Rust-native adapter. A status badge shows the connection state and backend name (UIA, ATSPI, or AX). After connecting, the tree is automatically captured. The connection bar disappears when connected and is replaced by Refresh and Disconnect buttons in the header.

assertions.description: A text input field is visible when disconnected, with placeholder 'Window title, pid:1234, or 'Desktop''. Pressing Enter in this field triggers connection.
A Connect button with a Plug icon is visible when disconnected. It is disabled when the target input is empty. During connection it shows 'Connecting...'.

Clicking Connect with a valid target (e.g., 'Notepad') invokes the a11y_connect Tauri command with backend='auto', then automatically captures the tree via a11y_capture. On success, the status badge changes from 'Disconnected' to the backend name (e.g., 'UIA'), the connection bar disappears, and the tree view appears. On failure, a red error message appears below the connection bar.
A Badge in the header shows 'Disconnected' (muted variant) when not connected, or the backend name in uppercase like 'UIA' (success variant) when connected
When connected, a Disconnect button with an Unplug icon appears in the header. Clicking it invokes a11y_disconnect, resets all state, and returns to the disconnected view with the target input.

When connection fails (e.g., target window not found), a red error message appears with a red-500/10 background and red-500/20 border below the connection bar, showing the error text from the Tauri command

groups.name: Snapshot Statistics Bar
groups.description: When connected with a captured tree, a stats bar shows the total node count, interactive node count, window title (if available), and generation number. This gives users a quick summary of the captured tree's scope.

assertions.description: The stats bar shows the total node count (e.g., '39 nodes') and interactive count (e.g., '18 interactive') as separate text spans
The stats bar shows the interactive node count (e.g., '18 interactive')
The stats bar shows the generation number (e.g., 'Gen 1') right-aligned, indicating how many captures have been performed

groups.name: Accessibility Tree Viewer
groups.description: The left panel shows a hierarchical tree of accessibility nodes captured from the target application. Each node is rendered as a treeitem with: an expand/collapse chevron (for nodes with children), a color-coded role badge (blue for buttons/links, green for inputs, gray for text, transparent for containers, purple for others), the accessible name, and a monospace ref ID (e.g., '@e3'). Interactive elements have a small blue dot indicator and a subtle blue background tint. Clicking a node selects it (highlighted with primary ring) and shows its details in the right panel. Keyboard navigation supports Enter/Space to select, ArrowRight to expand, ArrowLeft to collapse.

assertions.description: The tree view is contained in a Card with a 'Tree View' header featuring an Eye icon
The tree container has role='tree' and each node has role='treeitem' with proper aria-expanded and aria-selected attributes for accessibility compliance

Nodes with children show a chevron icon that toggles between ChevronRight (collapsed) and ChevronDown (expanded). Clicking the chevron expands or collapses the node's children. The root node and first-level children are expanded by default (depth < 1).
assertions.precondition: Connected with a captured tree that has nested nodes

assertions.description: Clicking a tree node selects it (shown with bg-primary/10 background and ring-1 ring-primary/30 border). The selected node's full details appear in the right panel. Only one node can be selected at a time.

Each tree node displays a Badge with the role name. Badges are color-coded: blue (info variant) for button/link/menuitem/tab, green (success) for edit/textbox/checkbox/radio/slider/combobox/spinbutton, gray (muted) for statictext/text/label/heading, default for containers (window/pane/group/list/tree/table/toolbar/menubar/dialog/tabpanel), purple for other roles.
Interactive nodes (is_interactive=true) show a small blue dot (w-1.5 h-1.5 rounded-full bg-blue-400) at the right edge and have a subtle blue background tint (bg-blue-500/5) when not selected
assertions.precondition: Connected with a tree containing interactive elements

assertions.description: A Refresh button with a RefreshCw icon appears in the header when connected. Clicking it re-invokes a11y_capture, replaces the tree, and clears the selected node. The icon spins while loading.

groups.name: Element Properties and Actions
groups.description: The right panel shows the selected node's full properties organized in sections: Identity (Role, Name, Value, Description, Ref ID with copy button, Source), Bounds (x, y, width, height in a 4-column grid), State (badges for all 13 state flags — active flags in green/success, inactive in outline), Supported Patterns (purple badges), and Actions (Click, Focus, Type buttons). When no node is selected, the panel shows 'Select a node to view details'.

assertions.description: The details panel is contained in a Card with a 'Details' header featuring a Search icon
When no node is selected, the details panel shows 'Select a node to view details' centered in muted text

criteria.textContains: Select a node to view details

assertions.description: The selected node's Ref ID (e.g., '@e3') is displayed in a monospace code element with a Copy button. Clicking Copy copies the ref ID to the clipboard.

State flags are displayed as badges: boolean flags (focused, disabled, hidden, readonly, required, editable, focusable, modal, multiselectable) always shown. TriBool flags (expanded, selected, checked, pressed) only shown when not 'n/a'. Active flags use success variant (green), inactive use outline variant.
A Click button with MousePointer icon invokes a11y_click with the selected node's ref ID. On success shows 'Action succeeded' in green. On failure shows the error in red.
A Focus button with Focus icon invokes a11y_focus with the selected node's ref ID

A 'Type...' button with Type icon reveals a text input field and Send button. Users enter text and press Send (or Enter) to invoke a11y_type_text with the ref ID, text, and clearFirst=false. The input disappears after sending.

After executing an action (Click/Focus/Type), the result is shown inline below the action buttons: green background (bg-green-500/10, text-green-400) for success ('Action succeeded'), red background (bg-red-500/10, text-red-400) for errors. Selecting a different node clears the action message.

groups.name: Query Panel
groups.description: The bottom Query tab provides a search interface for filtering the accessibility tree. Users select a role from a dropdown (25 common roles including button, checkbox, combobox, textbox, etc.), enter a label substring, toggle 'Interactive only', and click Search. Results appear as a clickable list showing role badge, name, and ref ID. Clicking a result selects it in the tree and shows its details.

assertions.description: The bottom tabbed section has a 'Query' tab that is selected by default

A role dropdown lets users filter by accessibility role. It includes 'Any role' as the default option plus 25 common roles: button, checkbox, combobox, dialog, edit, group, heading, link, list, listitem, menu, menuitem, pane, radio, slider, spinbutton, tab, tabpanel, text, textbox, toolbar, tree, treeitem, window.
A text input with placeholder 'Label contains...' lets users filter nodes whose accessible name contains the entered substring
An 'Interactive only' checkbox filters results to only interactive elements when checked

Clicking the Search button invokes a11y_query with the selected role, label substring, and interactive-only flag. Results appear as a scrollable list (max-h-40) of clickable rows showing role badge, name, and ref ID. Clicking a result selects it in the tree view and populates the details panel. When no results match, 'No results. Run a query above.' is shown.

groups.name: AI Context Panel
groups.description: The 'AI Context' tab shows the exact text representation that AI workflow agents receive when using the native_accessibility step type's ai_context action. Users click 'Generate AI Context' to invoke a11y_ai_context with maxElements=50 and interactiveOnly=true. The output appears in a monospace code block. A Copy button copies the text to the clipboard. This lets users verify exactly what the AI sees.

assertions.description: The bottom tabbed section has an 'AI Context' tab alongside the Query tab

A 'Generate AI Context' button with RefreshCw icon invokes a11y_ai_context. The icon spins while loading. The result appears in a <pre> element with monospace font, muted background, and border. The output follows the format: '## Accessibility Tree' header, optional URL/Title, '### Interactive Elements' section, then a list of '- @eN: role "name" [state]' entries.
After generating AI context, a Copy button appears that copies the entire text to the clipboard

groups.name: Visual Design and Styling
groups.description: The Accessibility Explorer uses the runner's standard design system: muted backgrounds for inputs (bg-muted/30), border-border for borders, primary color for active elements, foreground/muted-foreground for text hierarchy. Cards have border-border/30 header dividers. The overall page uses p-4 padding and gap-3 spacing between sections.

assertions.description: Text inputs use consistent styling: bg-muted/30 background, border-border border, text-foreground text color, text-muted-foreground/50 placeholder color, focus:ring-1 focus:ring-primary/50 focus state. This applies to the target input, label filter, and type-text input.

All text elements are legible against their backgrounds. The page title uses text-lg font-semibold. Stats bar uses text-xs text-muted-foreground. Tree node names use text-sm text-foreground. Ref IDs use font-mono text-[10px] text-muted-foreground/60. Detail labels use text-xs text-muted-foreground. No text should be invisible due to matching foreground/background colors.
Card headers (Tree View, Details) have a bottom border (border-b border-border/30) separating them from content. They use py-2 px-3 padding and text-xs font size for the title.

groups.name: Keyboard Navigation
groups.description: The tree view supports keyboard navigation: Tab to focus tree items, Enter or Space to select a node, ArrowRight to expand a collapsed node, ArrowLeft to collapse an expanded node. The target input supports Enter to submit. The type-text input supports Enter to send.

assertions.description: Tree items are focusable (tabIndex=0) and respond to keyboard: Enter/Space selects the node, ArrowRight expands (if collapsed and has children), ArrowLeft collapses (if expanded). Each treeitem has proper aria-expanded and aria-selected attributes.
The expand/collapse chevron buttons have aria-labels: 'Expand' when collapsed, 'Collapse' when expanded
assertions.precondition: Connected with a tree that has collapsed nodes

states.name: Disconnected
states.description: The initial state when the page loads. The header with 'Accessibility Explorer' title and 'Disconnected' badge is visible, the connection bar with target input and Connect button is shown, and the main area displays the empty-state message 'Connect to an application to explore its accessibility tree'. No tree, details, stats bar, or bottom tabs are visible.

transitions.name: User clicks Connect or presses Enter with a non-empty target

states.name: Connecting
states.description: The Connect button shows 'Connecting...' while the a11y_connect and a11y_capture Tauri commands are in flight. The target input remains visible but the user cannot submit again until the attempt resolves.

transitions.name: Connection fails (target not found or backend error)

states.name: Connection Error
states.description: The connection attempt failed. The page remains in disconnected layout but a red error message appears below the connection bar with the error text. The target input and Connect button remain available for retry.

transitions.name: User retries connection with a new or same target

states.name: Connected (No Selection)
states.description: Successfully connected to a target. The status badge shows the backend name (e.g., 'UIA'). The connection bar is hidden; Refresh and Disconnect buttons appear in the header. The stats bar shows node count, interactive count, and generation number. The two-column layout is visible: the tree view on the left with expandable nodes, and the details panel on the right showing 'Select a node to view details'. The bottom Query and AI Context tabs are available.

elements.textContains: Select a node to view details

transitions.name: User clicks Refresh to re-capture the tree

states.name: Refreshing Tree
states.description: The Refresh button's icon is spinning while a11y_capture re-captures the accessibility tree. The tree view and stats bar remain visible but will be replaced when the capture completes.

states.name: Connected (Node Selected)
states.description: A tree node is selected (highlighted with primary ring). The details panel shows the selected node's properties organized in sections: Identity (Role, Name, Value, Description, Ref ID with copy button, Source), Bounds (x, y, width, height), State (green/outline badges), Supported Patterns (purple badges), and Actions (Click, Focus, Type buttons). The tree view, stats bar, Refresh, and Disconnect buttons remain visible.

transitions.name: User clicks a different tree node
User clicks the Click action button
User clicks the Focus action button
User clicks the Type... button to reveal the text input
User clicks Refresh to re-capture the tree

states.name: Typing Action Input
states.description: The Type... button was clicked and a text input field with a Send button is now visible below the action buttons. The user can enter text and press Send or Enter to invoke a11y_type_text. The rest of the connected+selected UI remains visible.

transitions.name: User enters text and clicks Send or presses Enter

states.name: Action Result Displayed
states.description: An action (Click, Focus, or Type) has been executed and the result message is shown inline below the action buttons. A green message ('Action succeeded') on success or a red message with the error text on failure. The node remains selected. Selecting a different node clears this message and returns to the connected-node-selected state.

transitions.name: User selects a different tree node, clearing the action message
User executes another Click action on the same node
